# Production Readiness Assessment

## Well-Architected Framework (WAF) + Cloud Adoption Framework (CAF)

### EHDS Integration Hub

> Assessment date: 2026-03-25 | Based on load tests + codebase analysis

---

## Executive Summary

| Pillar                      | Score    | Status                                 |
| --------------------------- | -------- | -------------------------------------- |
| WAF: Operational Excellence | 4/10     | 🔴 Needs Work                          |
| WAF: Security               | 6/10     | 🟡 Partial                             |
| WAF: Reliability            | 5/10     | 🔴 Needs Work                          |
| WAF: Performance Efficiency | 4/10     | 🔴 Needs Work                          |
| WAF: Cost Optimization      | 5/10     | 🟡 Partial                             |
| WAF: Sustainability         | 3/10     | 🔴 Needs Work                          |
| CAF: Strategy & Plan        | 7/10     | 🟡 Good for MVP                        |
| CAF: Govern & Manage        | 4/10     | 🔴 Needs Work                          |
| **Overall**                 | **5/10** | **🟡 MVP-Ready, NOT Production-Ready** |

---

## WAF Pillar 1: Operational Excellence

### Current State

- ✅ Pre-commit hooks (Prettier, shellcheck, hadolint, TypeScript, ESLint)
- ✅ Automated E2E tests (Playwright) and unit tests (Vitest)
- ✅ DSP/DCP/EHDS compliance test scripts
- ✅ Structured seed scripts with phase control (`--from`, `--only`)
- ❌ No structured logging (no correlation IDs, no structured JSON logs)
- ❌ No distributed tracing (no OpenTelemetry)
- ❌ No alerting rules or on-call runbooks
- ❌ HashiCorp Vault in dev mode (in-memory, lost on restart)
- ❌ No CI/CD pipeline for K8s deployment (GitHub Actions only for Pages)
- ❌ No feature flags for phased rollouts

### Remediation Roadmap (Priority Order)

| Priority | Action                                                                        | Effort | Impact   |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------ | -------- |
| P0       | Vault: switch to file/integrated storage (not in-memory dev mode)             | 2d     | Critical |
| P0       | Add OpenTelemetry SDK to neo4j-proxy and UI (traces + metrics)                | 3d     | High     |
| P1       | Add structured logging (pino/winston with correlation IDs)                    | 2d     | High     |
| P1       | Create K8s Helm chart or Kustomize for all 19 services                        | 5d     | High     |
| P1       | Add GitHub Actions CI pipeline for K8s deployment to StackIT SKE              | 3d     | High     |
| P2       | Write operational runbooks (Vault recovery, Neo4j seed replay, EDC-V restart) | 3d     | Medium   |
| P2       | Add Prometheus metrics endpoint to neo4j-proxy (`/metrics`)                   | 1d     | Medium   |

---

## WAF Pillar 2: Security

### Current State

- ✅ Keycloak OIDC with 6 role-based scopes
- ✅ DID/VC-based participant identity (IdentityHub + IssuerService)
- ✅ DSP contract enforcement before data transfer
- ✅ ODRL policies on all DataProducts
- ✅ Route protection via Next.js middleware
- ✅ No secrets in codebase (Vault + env vars)
- ⚠️ Vault in dev mode (seal keys not persisted — P0 risk)
- ⚠️ Neo4j Community: no role-based DB access control (single user)
- ⚠️ Neo4j proxy has no rate limiting (exhaustion possible)
- ❌ No network policies (K8s pods can talk to each other freely)
- ❌ No OWASP ZAP / security scan in CI
- ❌ CORS policy not verified under load
- ❌ No audit log rotation/retention policy (EHDS requires 10-year retention)
- ❌ No mTLS between internal services (relies on Docker network trust)
- ❌ k-anonymity in federated query (`/federated/query`) not validated at scale

### Remediation Roadmap

| Priority | Action                                                                          | Effort | Impact            |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------ | ----------------- |
| P0       | Vault persistent storage (Raft or file backend)                                 | 2d     | Critical          |
| P0       | Add rate limiting to neo4j-proxy (express-rate-limit: 100 req/min/IP)           | 0.5d   | Critical          |
| P0       | Enforce k-anonymity threshold in production (min_cohort_size ≥ 5)               | 1d     | Critical (GDPR)   |
| P1       | Add K8s NetworkPolicies (deny-all default, allow-list per service)              | 2d     | High              |
| P1       | Enable Neo4j role-based access (upgrade to Enterprise OR use proxy-only access) | 3d     | High              |
| P1       | Add OWASP ZAP scan to CI                                                        | 1d     | High              |
| P1       | Configure audit log retention (10 years, EHDS Art. 50)                          | 2d     | High (Compliance) |
| P2       | mTLS between internal services via Istio or Linkerd                             | 5d     | Medium            |
| P2       | Rotate Keycloak client secrets on schedule                                      | 1d     | Medium            |

---

## WAF Pillar 3: Reliability

### Current State (from load tests)

- ✅ Neo4j proxy: 99%+ success at 200 VUs, handles 348 RPS at 600 VUs
- ✅ Lightweight UI routes: stable up to 600 VUs
- ❌ **CRITICAL: `/api/graph` crashes Next.js at ~90 concurrent requests**
  - Root cause: 60MB+ JSON payload per response (5,300+ nodes serialised)
  - Fix: paginate graph API or return aggregated summary + lazy-load
- ❌ No health check retries or circuit breakers
- ❌ Neo4j Community Edition: no clustering, no automatic failover
- ❌ Docker volumes not backed up automatically
- ❌ No graceful shutdown handling in neo4j-proxy (in-flight requests dropped)
- ❌ Vault restart loses all secrets (requires full re-bootstrap)
- ❌ No readiness/liveness probes configured for K8s

### Remediation Roadmap

| Priority | Action                                                                     | Effort | Impact   |
| -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------ | -------- |
| P0       | **Fix graph API**: add pagination (`?page=&limit=`) + node-level lazy load | 3d     | Critical |
| P0       | Add K8s readiness + liveness probes for all services                       | 1d     | Critical |
| P0       | Persistent Vault storage (see Security P0)                                 | 2d     | Critical |
| P1       | Add circuit breaker to neo4j-proxy (opossum library)                       | 1d     | High     |
| P1       | Configure Neo4j automatic backup to object storage (daily)                 | 2d     | High     |
| P1       | Add graceful shutdown to neo4j-proxy (drain connections on SIGTERM)        | 0.5d   | High     |
| P2       | Neo4j Enterprise or Fabric for HA (if budget allows)                       | 5d     | Medium   |
| P2       | Multi-region active-passive failover via StackIT                           | 8d     | Medium   |

---

## WAF Pillar 4: Performance Efficiency

### Current State (from load tests)

- ✅ Neo4j proxy p95=16ms (catalog), p95=15ms (OMOP) — excellent
- ✅ OMOP cohort aggregation: 80ms average, scales to 200+ VUs
- ✅ No N+1 queries observed in proxy (single Cypher queries)
- ❌ Graph API: 60MB payload → 1.75s p50, 22s p95, crashes at 90 VUs
- ❌ Patient API: p95=8.5s at 200 VUs (Neo4j query not optimized)
- ❌ No response caching (catalog is static, could be cached 60s)
- ❌ No compression (gzip/brotli) on API responses
- ❌ No Neo4j query result caching (APOC cache not configured)
- ❌ Neo4j heap max 1GB: with 5300+ nodes, this is tight under concurrent load
- ❌ No CDN for static UI assets

### Remediation Roadmap

| Priority | Action                                                                               | Effort | Impact   |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------ | -------- |
| P0       | Paginate `/api/graph` (return 200 nodes/page, client renders incrementally)          | 3d     | Critical |
| P1       | Add HTTP response compression (next.config.js `compress: true`, Express compression) | 0.5d   | High     |
| P1       | Cache catalog response (Redis or in-memory, 60s TTL)                                 | 1d     | High     |
| P1       | Increase Neo4j heap to 2GB + page cache to 4GB in production                         | 0.5d   | High     |
| P1       | Add Neo4j indexes for all FHIR query paths (Patient.fhirId, Condition.code)          | 1d     | High     |
| P2       | APOC query result caching for expensive traversals                                   | 2d     | Medium   |
| P2       | Add CDN (Cloudflare or StackIT CDN) for static UI assets                             | 2d     | Medium   |

### Performance targets (production K8s, after fixes)

| Scenario                     | Target RPS | p95 Target |
| ---------------------------- | ---------- | ---------- |
| 200 participants (sustained) | 40 RPS     | <500ms     |
| 200 participants (peak 5×)   | 200 RPS    | <2s        |
| 1,000 participants (scaled)  | 200 RPS    | <1s        |

---

## WAF Pillar 5: Cost Optimization

### Current State

- ✅ Neo4j Community (free, vs Enterprise ≥€15k/year)
- ✅ Docker Compose minimises cloud cost for dev/test
- ❌ Vault dev mode wipes secrets → forced full re-bootstrap = ops cost
- ❌ No autoscaling (HPA) configured for stateless services
- ❌ Graph API data transfer: 60MB × N requests = high egress cost
- ❌ No cost tagging strategy for tenant isolation billing

### Remediation Roadmap

| Priority                    | Action                                      | Monthly Saving     |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ------------------ |
| P0                          | Fix graph API payload (pagination)          | €90/month egress   |
| P1                          | Enable gzip on all APIs                     | €78/month egress   |
| P1                          | HPA for neo4j-proxy (min 1, max 5 replicas) | €150/month compute |
| P1                          | Spot nodes for app pool (3× c1.xlarge)      | €78/month compute  |
| P2                          | CDN for static assets                       | €40/month egress   |
| **Total potential savings** |                                             | **~€436/month**    |

---

## WAF Pillar 6: Sustainability

### Current State

- ❌ No carbon-aware scheduling
- ❌ No idle-down of non-production environments
- ❌ No resource utilisation reporting
- ❌ Graph API wastes 60MB of compute + network per request

### Recommendations

1. Use StackIT's DE-FRA-1 region (Schwarz Group targets 100% renewable energy)
2. Auto-shutdown dev/staging environments outside business hours (saves ~60% dev cost)
3. Fix graph API — reduces CPU + network by ~70% per graph view
4. Set Neo4j page cache limits properly (avoid OS memory pressure)
5. Use HPA + KEDA for event-driven scaling (scale to zero during off-hours)

---

## CAF Assessment

### Strategy & Plan (7/10)

- ✅ Clear EHDS regulatory motivation
- ✅ FHIR R4, OMOP CDM, DSP alignment
- ✅ Fictional participants (trademark policy documented)
- ✅ Phased seeding approach (7 phases, resumable)
- ❌ No formal SLA defined for dataspace participants
- ❌ No data governance policy registry beyond ODRL policies

### Ready (5/10)

- ✅ All services containerised
- ✅ Working local dev stack
- ❌ No K8s manifests / Helm chart
- ❌ No StackIT SKE configuration
- ❌ Vault not production-ready

### Adopt (6/10)

- ✅ DSP 2025-1 TCK compliance tests
- ✅ DCP v1.0 compliance
- ✅ EHDS domain tests
- ❌ No chaos engineering (no resilience testing)
- ❌ No data migration runbook for version upgrades

### Govern & Manage (4/10)

- ❌ No cost allocation tags per tenant
- ❌ No EHDS audit log retention policy (required: 10 years)
- ❌ No incident response plan
- ❌ No change management process
- ❌ No SLA monitoring dashboard
- ⚠️ k-anonymity not enforced by policy (code-level only)

---

## Consolidated P0 Blockers (Must fix before production)

| #                   | Issue                                                   | Effort   | WAF Pillar                |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------- |
| 1                   | Graph API crashes at 90 concurrent users (60MB payload) | 3d       | Reliability + Performance |
| 2                   | Vault dev mode loses secrets on restart                 | 2d       | Reliability + Security    |
| 3                   | No rate limiting on neo4j-proxy                         | 0.5d     | Security                  |
| 4                   | k-anonymity not enforced by policy (federated query)    | 1d       | Security (GDPR)           |
| 5                   | No K8s readiness/liveness probes                        | 1d       | Reliability               |
| 6                   | EHDS audit log retention policy missing                 | 2d       | Governance                |
| **Total P0 effort** |                                                         | **~10d** |                           |

## Consolidated P1 (Production hardening, sprint 2)

Total effort: **~25 developer-days**

## Timeline to Production-Ready

| Phase                   | Duration     | Deliverables                                                     |
| ----------------------- | ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Sprint 1 (P0 fixes)     | 2 weeks      | Graph pagination, Vault persistence, rate limiting, K8s probes   |
| Sprint 2 (P1 hardening) | 3 weeks      | OTel, structured logging, compression, caching, network policies |
| Sprint 3 (K8s deploy)   | 2 weeks      | Helm chart, CI/CD to StackIT SKE, full load test on cloud        |
| Sprint 4 (Compliance)   | 2 weeks      | Audit retention, OWASP scan, chaos testing, runbooks             |
| **Total**               | **~9 weeks** | Production-ready EHDS dataspace                                  |

docs.markdown:
# Operational guideline: hosting the hub and Klarbefund under the EHDS and the BSI standards

What is in this repository is a demonstrator: one Azure resource group, one
operator, fictional participants, synthetic patients, and a stack that stops
at night to stay inside a personal credit. This guideline is written for the
day someone hosts it for real: a health data access body, an operating
company working for one, a health insurer, a hospital group, or a vendor who
takes the white-label app. It says which role in Regulation (EU) 2025/327
(the EHDS) operates which part, what the BSI standards require of each part,
and what has to change from the demo before any real health data touches it.

Article numbers are those of the adopted Regulation. Older files in this
repository still carry the numbers of the 2022 proposal; the mapping is in
[`docs/ehds-article-numbering.md`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ehds-article-numbering.md). The
evidence behind every "the demo already does" below is in the
[security test report](/docs/security/security-test-report), the two threat
models ([hub](/docs/security/threat-model-hub), [app](/docs/security/threat-model-klarbefund)), the
[C5 gap analysis](/docs/security/bsi-c5-gap-analysis) and the Klarbefund
[self-assessment](/docs/security/klarbefund-self-assessment). This document is a
guideline by the project, not legal advice and not a certification.

## 1. The roles in the EHDS, and who operates what

The Regulation names the roles; it does not say who runs the servers below
the access body. The hub's seven Keycloak roles are the technical shadow of
the legal roles, and the table says which legal actor stands behind each
technical one when the system leaves the demo.

| EHDS role (Reg. 2025/327)                                                                                           | What the Regulation expects of it                                                                                                                                                           | Hub role / component                                                                                   | Who operates it in a real deployment                                                                                                             |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Natural person** (the patient), Art. 3 to 10, opt-out Art. 71                                                     | Access to their own electronic health data, insertion, rectification, restriction, information on who accessed; the right to opt out of secondary use.                                      | `PATIENT`; `/patient/*`; Klarbefund on the phone; EUDI wallet sign-in (ADR-028)                        | Themselves, through the access service of the digital health authority or an EHR system; the app is theirs, the operator never sees its content. |

### The operating model as a process

The diagram is a BPMN-style process with one swimlane per role: boxes are
tasks, diamonds are decisions, the loop at the end is the output control,
the green dots are start and end. Article numbers are the adopted ones. The
lanes of the holder, the user and the person are their own; the access
body's lane is where every decision sits; the operating company's and the
SPE operator's lanes hold the technical work that this repository
implements.

![EHDS operating model: one swimlane per role, from the holder's onboarding through application, permit, opt-out, extraction, the secure processing environment and output control to the published results](__BASE_PATH__/published-docs/ehds-operating-model.svg)

Source: [`diagrams/ehds-operating-model.puml`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/security/diagrams/ehds-operating-model.puml), rendered with `scripts/render-plantuml.sh`.

Three responsibilities that the diagram makes visible and a contract must
repeat: the access body decides and the operator executes; the person's
opt-out reaches the holder's extraction through the operator's policy
evaluation, not through goodwill; and no output leaves the SPE on the
operator's say-so, only on the access body's.

Two things follow. **Controllership is never the operator's.** The access
body is controller for the SPE and the permit data (Art. 74); the holder is
controller of its source data; the operator processes on instruction. Every
hosting contract repeats this. **Role grants are decisions, not tickets.**
Who becomes `HDAB_AUTHORITY` or `TRUST_CENTER_OPERATOR` is decided by the
access body in writing; the operator executes the grant in Keycloak and the
grant is logged (ADR-045). The demo assigns roles in a seed file; a real
deployment removes the seed and keeps the grant history.

## 4. Identity and access

- **One identity provider, operated by the platform operator, with the
  realm in version control.** Keycloak holds the roles; the hub trusts only
  the roles in the token (`ui/src/lib/auth.ts`). Every API route needs a
  session (ADR-044); the one exception per route is written as an ADR, never
  as a configuration flag.
- **Organisations prove who they are with verifiable credentials** issued
  against an authoritative register (DCP v1.0, `did:web`). The IssuerService
  is the operator's; the holder's keys stay in the holder's Vault
  namespace. The demo's seed issues credentials to fictional organisations;
  a real deployment issues them only after the onboarding steps in the
  operating-company document, step 3.
- **Natural persons sign in through the EUDI wallet or the national eID**,
  at assurance "high" for their own record (Art. 16 identification
  management; TR-03107). Username and password remain for staff, with MFA,
  and never for patients.
- **Privileged roles** (`EDC_ADMIN`, `HDAB_AUTHORITY`,
  `TRUST_CENTER_OPERATOR`) require MFA, a named person, a documented grant by
  the access body, and a review every quarter. Service accounts (the
  catalogue crawler's token, ADR-020; the app's sandbox account, ADR-054) are
  listed with owner, scope and rotation date.
- **The Keycloak admin console is not on the internet** (finding F10, the
  Caddy guard in `scripts/azure/guard-keycloak-console.sh`); administration
  goes through a private network or a bastion with session recording.
- **Sessions** are short for privileged roles, bound to the client, and
  revoked on role change. `NEXTAUTH_SECRET` and every other operator secret
  is a Key Vault reference (ADR-036), rotated on a schedule.
- **Who sees a patient's identity is decided by role, never by a
  parameter** (`ui/src/lib/patient-identity.ts`): holders and the platform
  operator for primary use, the patient for their own record only
  (`refuseForeignRecord`), everyone else a pseudonym. The NLQ proxy refuses
  identity-revealing queries. This stays as it is and is tested on every
  build.

## 5. Data protection

- **Controllership and contracts.** The access body is controller for the
  secure processing environment (Art. 74) and processor-instructs the
  operator; the holder is controller of its source data; the data user is
  controller of what it is permitted to process, inside the SPE only. Each
  pair signs an Art. 28 GDPR contract; the operating-company document gives
  the model.
- **A data protection impact assessment** before go-live, for the platform
  as a whole and for the SPE separately. The two threat models are the
  technical input; the DPIA adds the legal basis per data category (Art. 51)
  and the residual risks.
- **Data minimisation and purpose limitation** (Art. 66): the access body
  decides for each permit whether anonymised data answer the question, and
  only then pseudonymised data. The hub's OMOP aggregates and the k-anonymity
  of the cohort views are the anonymised path; the FHIR extraction is the
  pseudonymised one and runs only inside the SPE.
- **Pseudonymisation keys** are held by the access body or a trusted third
  party, never by the data user and never by the operator of the SPE.
- **The opt-out** (Art. 71) is a register the access body keeps; the
  holder's connector checks it before extraction. The demo has consent
  records in the app and on the patient page; a real deployment wires the
  national opt-out register into the ODRL policy evaluation.
- **Patient rights for primary use** (Art. 3 to 10): access, insertion,
  rectification, restriction, and the list of who accessed. The patient
  page's access log and the audit trail (ADR-045) are the implementation;
  the operator must answer a request within the GDPR month.
- **Residency.** Every processor is in the EU or EEA; the explanation
  service's model provider is chosen by region and quota (ADR-035), and the
  on-device model is the default so that no health value leaves the phone
  unless the person sends it.
- **The app** holds nothing the operator can read: values, pages and
  diagnostics are encrypted per record with a key in the Secure Enclave,
  excluded from backups, behind Face ID or the passcode (ADR-060). The
  white-label operator inherits this; it must not add telemetry that
  carries values.

## 6. Logging, retention and the audit trail

What must be logged, for how long, and who may read it. The project's
[audit retention policy](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/audit-retention-policy.md) holds the current
numbers (it still cites the proposal's article numbers); the duties come
from Art. 57 (the access body keeps a record of applications and permits),
Art. 73 (every access to the SPE and every output logged), Art. 58 and 59
(information to the public, annual report) and GDPR accountability.

| Event                                                       | Logged by                          | Readable by                                            | Retention (project policy)                     |
| ----------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------- |
| Data access, transfer, contract (the `TransferEvent` chain) | The neo4j-proxy and the connectors | The access body, the holder for its data, auditors     | 10 years                                       |
| Permit decisions, revocations                               | The access body in the hub         | Public register for the decision, parties for the file | 10 years                                       |
| SPE sessions: who, which dataset, which query, which output | The SPE                            | The access body; the data user for its own             | 10 years                                       |
| Role grants and revocations, privileged sign-ins            | Keycloak, shipped to the SIEM      | The operator's security team, auditors                 | 2 years, longer if an incident references them |
| HTTP access at the edge, authentication events              | The edge and Keycloak              | The operator's security team                           | 2 years                                        |
| Patient's own record: every read, by whom                   | The hub                            | The patient, on their page                             | As long as the record                          |
| App: diagnostics the person chooses to export               | The app, on the device only        | The person; the developers only if sent                | The person decides                             |

Three rules the demo already keeps and a real deployment must keep:
the audit trail is written by the service that performed the action, not by
the client; it is append-only for everyone but the retention job
(DIP-06, implement with an immutable store or a signed chain); and no log
line carries a health value or a name where a pseudonym does.

## 8. Operating the platform

- **Change management.** Every change is a pull request with the gates in
  `docs/quality-gates.md`: type-check, lint, unit and journey tests, the
  Bruno collection against the hub, Semgrep, gitleaks, hadolint, the SBOM
  check, CodeQL for TypeScript and Swift, trivy and grype. Merges deploy
  through `deploy-azure.yml` from `main` only; the production environment
  adds a release approval by the operator's change board and a signed image.
- **Vulnerability management.** The scans in `scripts/security/scan-repo.sh`
  run on every push and nightly; high and critical findings are fixed within
  the contract's window or time-boxed with a written exception. The
  [security test report](/docs/security/security-test-report) is repeated at
  every release and once a year by an independent tester.
- **Patching.** Base images rebuilt monthly and on advisories; Keycloak,
  Neo4j and Postgres on supported major versions (ADR-030 for Neo4j, the
  Postgres 16 to 17 runbook for the pattern).
- **Backups and recovery.** Postgres with point-in-time restore across
  zones; Neo4j with daily backups and a restore test every quarter; Vault's
  state is on Postgres (ADR-046) and the unseal keys in Key Vault with a
  documented recovery drill. Targets to agree in the contract: recovery
  point one hour, recovery time four hours for the hub, one working day for
  the SPE.
- **Availability.** 24x7; the demo's schedule is removed; health checks in
  every image (finding F6) and probes in every app definition; two replicas
  for the hub and the proxy; the off-hours page becomes a maintenance page
  used only inside announced windows.
- **Key management.** Signing keys for credentials in an HSM; TLS
  certificates automated; every secret rotated at least yearly and on
  personnel change; the break-glass procedure with two-person approval and a
  log.
- **Supplier security** (C5 OIS-05): Keycloak, Neo4j, the EDC components,
  the cloud and the model provider assessed and listed with their
  attestations; the bills of materials in `docs/sbom/` are the inventory.
- **Exit.** Data export in FHIR R4 and OMOP CDM is already the hub's
  interface; the contract names the format, the time and the deletion
  evidence at the end.

## 9. Klarbefund in a white-label deployment

The app changes owner but not architecture. The entity that places it on
the market:

- keeps the on-device default: values, pages and the explanation stay on the
  phone unless the person sends them (self-assessment O.Purp, O.Data);
- keeps the app lock and the encryption per record (ADR-060, O.Auth,
  O.Cryp) and does not add analytics that see values;
- operates the sandbox-account service (ADR-054) and, if offered, the
  explanation service (ADR-034, ADR-035) in the EU under its own name and
  its own DPIA;
- publishes a privacy notice in the person's language and a vulnerability
  disclosure address;
- commissions the TR-03161 test and, if it claims interoperability with an
  EHR system, the Art. 48 declaration; it does not claim DiGA status without
  the CE mark the DiGA route requires (self-assessment, "Regulation");
- repeats the accuracy evidence on its own report formats before the pilot
  (the benchmark in [`evidence.md`](/docs/security/klarbefund-evidence) is synthetic).

| 15  | Opt-out register wired into policy evaluation                                             | Access body, operator              | Policy test with an opted-out record                                                       |
| 16  | Vulnerability disclosure address published; supplier list with attestations               | Operator                           | `SECURITY.md`, supplier register                                                           |

## 11. What the demonstrator does not do

So that nobody reads more into it than is there:

- It is one tenant, one operator, one region, stopped at night.
- Its participants, access bodies and patients are fictional; its credentials
  are issued by its own issuer against no register.
- It has no SIEM, no WAF, no customer-managed keys, no backup of the graph,
  no MFA, and the secure processing environment is a set of views on the same
  database, not an isolated environment (ADR-037 and ADR-052 record what was
  assessed).
- It has had no independent penetration test and no TR-03161 test; the
  [security test report](/docs/security/security-test-report) is the project
  testing itself.
- Its EHDS article references are partly the proposal's numbers; this
  document uses the adopted ones.

What it does have is the shape, the roles, the logging, the role-based
identity rules, the connectors and the exports that a real deployment
needs, with every decision written as an ADR and every claim tied to a test.
That is what makes it a reference and not a product.

## Sources

- Regulation (EU) 2025/327 on the European Health Data Space, OJ L, 5 March 2025.
- Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR), Art. 28, 33, 34, 35.
- Directive (EU) 2022/2555 (NIS2) and its national transposition.
- BSI, Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue C5:2020.
- BSI, IT-Grundschutz-Kompendium, current edition; BSI Standards 200-1 to 200-3.
- BSI TR-02102-1 and TR-02102-2, cryptographic mechanisms and TLS.
- BSI TR-03161, security requirements for digital health applications, parts 1 to 3.
- BSI TR-03116-4, cryptographic requirements for federal projects, TLS.
- BSI TR-03107-1, electronic identities and trust services in e-government.
- This repository: the ADRs cited above, `docs/ehds-operating-company.md`,
  `docs/audit-retention-policy.md`, `docs/ehds-article-numbering.md`.

# Security test report, 2026-10-15

A self-conducted security test of the Klarbefund app and the demo hub, by
the project, with the tools the repository can run: static analysis,
dependency and container scanning, secret scanning, configuration tests
and anonymous black-box checks of the live hub. **It is not an independent
penetration test.** What such a test would add is listed at the end. Every
number here is reproducible with the commands given; the raw reports of this
run are not committed (they carry paths), the scripts are.

| Item         | Value                                                                                                                                           |
| ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Commit       | `64737039` on `feat/186-insurer-report` (the fixes below were made on the same branch)                                                          |
| Date         | 2026-10-15, 18:34 to 18:58 UTC                                                                                                                  |
| Machine      | macOS 26.7.1, Xcode 26 (Swift 6.4), syft 1.51.1, grype 0.118.0, trivy 0.74.0, gitleaks 8.30.1, semgrep 1.176.0, CodeQL CLI                      |
| Scope        | `clients/ios` (the app), `ui`, `services/*`, the Dockerfiles, the Kubernetes manifests, the live hub `ehds.mabu.red` from outside               |
| Not in scope | The EDC connectors and Keycloak internals (the hub's own threat model, `threat-model.md`), Apple's platform, the model providers behind ADR-034 |

## Method

| Layer                  | Tool, what it checked                                                                                | Command                                                      |
| ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Static analysis, Swift | CodeQL, security queries over 31 app and 51 Shared files                                             | `clients/ios/Scripts/codeql-swift.sh`                        |
| Static analysis, TS/JS | CodeQL in CI on every push (`codeql.yml`); Semgrep with the repository's own rules locally           | `scripts/security/scan-repo.sh`                              |
| Dependencies           | syft bills of materials, grype and npm audit against them                                            | `scripts/security/generate-sbom.sh`, `scan-repo.sh`          |
| Filesystem             | trivy: vulnerabilities, secrets, misconfiguration in Dockerfiles and Kubernetes manifests            | `scan-repo.sh`                                               |
| Secrets                | gitleaks over the tree and the last 200 commits                                                      | `scan-repo.sh`                                               |
| Build configuration    | `SecurityPostureTests` (9 tests): entitlements, privacy manifest, ATS, cryptography, PKCE, HealthKit | `cd clients/ios && swift test --filter SecurityPostureTests` |
| Behaviour              | The unit suites: 419 Swift tests, 2488 UI tests, 22 proxy tests on this branch                       | `swift test`, `npm test`                                     |
| Live hub, anonymous    | 40 black-box checks: route gates, redirects, dotfiles, CORS, headers, TLS versions, Keycloak console | `scripts/security/check-hub-blackbox.sh`                     |

## Results

| Check                                               | Result                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| CodeQL, Swift                                       | 0 findings, 0 accepted                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Semgrep, local rules                                | 0 findings                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| grype over the five bills                           | 0 matches (ui 530 components, proxy 180, epa-ingest 29, claude-federation 20, app 20 Apple frameworks, 0 third-party)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| npm audit, production, four lockfiles               | 0 critical, 0 high, 0 moderate, 0 low                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| trivy, vulnerabilities                              | 0 after the fix below (6 before, all in one Python package of the guideline scripts)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| trivy, secrets                                      | 0                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| trivy, misconfiguration                             | 0 after the fixes (3 HIGH, 2 MEDIUM and 12 LOW before; the last ten, the missing health checks of F6, closed 2026-10-16)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| gitleaks, tree                                      | 0 after review (2 before, both reviewed and allowlisted with the reason)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| gitleaks, last 200 commits                          | 0                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| hadolint                                            | 5 info, 0 warning, 0 error                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| shellcheck, error severity                          | 0                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| SecurityPostureTests                                | 9 of 9 pass                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Unit suites                                         | all pass                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Live hub, black-box (second run, online, 20:37 UTC) | 44 of 46 checks pass: every API route refuses an anonymous caller (401), protected pages redirect, no dotfile served, no CORS reflection, all five security headers, TLS 1.0 and 1.1 refused, metrics closed. Two fails: one expectation of the script (a route that does not exist, fixed) and F10 below                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Live hub, black-box                                 | **not run to completion**: the hub was in off-hours mode (ADR-053, stops 18:13 UTC), every API route answered 503 and the script exits 3 by design. Repeat Mon to Fri 05:17 to 18:13 UTC. What the run did establish: TLS 1.0 and 1.1 refused, 1.2 and 1.3 offered (ECDHE, ChaCha20-Poly1305), certificate valid to 2027-02-08; no CORS origin reflected; Keycloak admin console, metrics and health not reachable from the internet (404); the dotfiles a scanner tries are rewritten to the offline page, not served |

## Findings

| #   | Severity       | Finding                                                                                                                                                                                        | Where                                                                  | Action                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| --- | -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| F1  | High           | `docling` 2.131.0 with three published advisories (two high)                                                                                                                                   | `scripts/leitlinien/uv.lock`                                           | **Fixed**: `uv lock --upgrade-package docling`, now 2.139.0; grype and trivy report 0                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| F2  | High (scanner) | Three Dockerfiles without a `USER` instruction (trivy DS-0002)                                                                                                                                 | `load-tests/azure`, `jad/keycloak-theme`, `scripts/azure/vault-unseal` | **Fixed**: the k6 and Keycloak images already ran unprivileged, now stated; the vault-unseal sidecar drops to `vault` after its root-only `apk add`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| F3  | Low            | gitleaks: IdentityHub superuser key in the compose stack's env file                                                                                                                            | `jad/issuerservice.env` (tracked)                                      | **Reviewed**: the published development default of the local JAD stack; Azure takes keys from Vault (ADR-046). Allowlisted with the reason in `.gitleaks.toml`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| F4  | Info           | gitleaks: a public search key of the AWMF guideline register embedded in a fetch script                                                                                                        | `scripts/leitlinien/fetch_index.py`                                    | **Reviewed**: the register's own public page embeds it; grants nothing a browser lacks. Allowlisted with the reason                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| F5  | Medium         | Kubernetes manifest: image tag `:latest` and a ConfigMap flagged as sensitive content                                                                                                          | `k8s/health-dataspace-ui.yaml`                                         | **Fixed 2026-10-15**: tag pinned to the package version; the flagged ConfigMap keys are a public client id and issuer URL (the secrets already sit in the Secret), recorded as a reviewed false positive in `.trivyignore`; trivy reports 0 on the manifest                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| F6  | Closed         | No `HEALTHCHECK` in ten Dockerfiles                                                                                                                                                            | `ui`, `services/*`, `scripts/azure/*`, others                          | **Fixed 2026-10-16**: every image carries a `HEALTHCHECK` matched to what it serves: the hub's `/api/health`, the proxy's and the explanation service's `/health`, the crawlers' Prometheus endpoint, Keycloak's `/health/ready` and Grafana's `/api/health` through a bash socket (neither image has curl), `vault status` for the unseal sidecar; the two one-shot jobs say `HEALTHCHECK NONE`. Container Apps still takes its probes from the app definition. trivy reports 0 misconfigurations over the repository                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| F7  | Low            | Kubernetes manifest runs with UID and GID below 10000                                                                                                                                          | `k8s/health-dataspace-ui.yaml`                                         | **Fixed 2026-10-15**: runs as 10001                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| F8  | Observe        | On the off-hours page the response carried Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy but not HSTS, X-Frame-Options or X-Content-Type-Options, although `next.config` sets all five for every path | `ehds.mabu.red/`, off hours                                            | **Closed 2026-10-15 20:37 UTC**: online, all five headers are present on `/`; only the off-hours page lacked them                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| F10 | Closed         | Keycloak admin console reachable from the internet: `auth.ehds.mabu.red/admin/master/console/` answers 200 (login still required; found when the black-box checks ran online at 20:37 UTC)     | Keycloak ingress                                                       | **Fix scripted**: `scripts/azure/guard-keycloak-console.sh` adds a Caddy sidecar that answers 403 for `/admin/*/console/*` and proxies the rest, keeping the admin REST API (which the hub and the provisioning scripts use with a token) reachable; Keycloak's own docs say hostname-admin does not block the console. **Applied and verified 2026-10-15 21:19 UTC**: with Keycloak started briefly behind the guard, discovery 200, the console paths 403, the admin REST API 401 without a token, the token endpoint answering, and `check-keycloak-health.sh` reporting the realm served from a working database; then stopped again. Rollback: the definition saved under `~/.mvhd/keycloak-rollback/` |
| F9  | Closed         | No app lock, no jailbreak detection, no certificate pinning in the app                                                                                                                         | `clients/ios`                                                          | **Decided 2026-10-15 (ADR-060)**: app lock implemented, on by default; pinning and jailbreak detection declined with reasons                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |

## What an independent test would add

This report is the project testing itself with deterministic tools. It
does not replace, and the self-assessment does not claim, an independent
penetration test. Such a test, by a BSI-recognised laboratory or a
contracted tester, would add:

1. **A release build on a device**: runtime inspection of the Keychain
   items, the sealed store and the file protection classes with the phone
   locked and unlocked; the cable test repeated by someone else.
2. **Authenticated black-box testing of the hub** as each of the seven
   roles, in office hours: horizontal access between patients (`refuseForeignRecord`), the
   app token's scope, rate limits under load, the App Attest verification
   with a replayed or forged attestation.
3. **The TR-03161 part 1 requirement list**, item by item against the
   official document, which this project assesses only at the level of its
   objective groups (`docs/klarbefund/self-assessment.md`).
4. **Keycloak and EDC configuration review** beyond what the public
   endpoints show.

Until then, the status in the self-assessment reads "tested by the
project, independent test open", and this document is the evidence for
the first half of that sentence.

# Threat Model — EHDS Integration Hub

**STRIDE analysis for the demo/MVP phase.**
Scope: UI (Next.js), Neo4j graph, DSP 2025-1 contract flow, DCP v1.0 credential exchange.

---

## System Context

```
Browser ──HTTPS──► Next.js UI ──bolt/HTTP──► Neo4j 5
                        │
                        ├─ /api/admin/*   (EDC_ADMIN only)
                        ├─ /api/patient/* (PATIENT only)
                        └─ /api/*         (authenticated)
                        │
              Keycloak 24 (OIDC)
              └─ realm: edcv  (7 personas)

DSP flow:  ConsumerEDC ──HTTP──► ProviderEDC
DCP flow:  Wallet ──HTTP──► CredentialService ──► TrustCenter
```

---

## Assets

| Asset                  | Sensitivity | Notes                                 |
| ---------------------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------- |
| Patient FHIR records   | HIGH        | Synthetic in demo; real in production |
| Neo4j credentials      | HIGH        | Hardcoded defaults in dev only        |
| Keycloak client secret | HIGH        | `KEYCLOAK_SECRET` env var             |
| NEXTAUTH_SECRET        | HIGH        | JWT signing key                       |
| Verifiable Credentials | MEDIUM      | Participant DIDs + attestations       |
| Contract / policy data | MEDIUM      | ODRL policies, transfer agreements    |
| Audit log              | MEDIUM      | Access provenance records             |
| Graph topology         | LOW         | Schema is public documentation        |

---

## STRIDE Analysis

### Spoofing

| ID   | Threat                      | Component          | Demo Mitigation              | Production Mitigation                 |
| ---- | --------------------------- | ------------------ | ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| S-01 | Impersonate participant DID | DSP negotiation    | DID:web anchored to domain   | DNSSEC + DID rotation policy          |
| S-02 | Forge JWT session           | Next.js API routes | `NEXTAUTH_SECRET` required   | Short-lived tokens + refresh rotation |
| S-03 | Replay VC presentation      | DCP exchange       | Presentation timestamp check | Nonce-based challenge-response        |
| S-04 | Keycloak realm takeover     | Keycloak           | Admin credentials restricted | Separate realm per env + MFA on admin |

### Tampering

| ID   | Threat                             | Component           | Demo Mitigation                         | Production Mitigation              |
| ---- | ---------------------------------- | ------------------- | --------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| T-01 | Cypher injection via audit filters | `/api/admin/audit`  | **✅ Parameterised queries (D1)**       | Same + WAF                         |
| T-02 | Modify contract terms in transit   | DSP HTTP            | HTTPS only (TLS 1.2+)                   | mTLS between EDC connectors        |
| T-03 | Tamper with VC claims              | DCP                 | VC signature verified                   | Hardware HSM for issuer key        |
| T-04 | CSRF on state-changing API calls   | Next.js POST routes | SameSite=Lax cookies (NextAuth default) | CSRF tokens on sensitive mutations |

### Repudiation

| ID   | Threat                      | Component       | Demo Mitigation                        | Production Mitigation                 |
| ---- | --------------------------- | --------------- | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| R-01 | Deny data transfer occurred | Neo4j audit log | `DataTransfer` + `TransferEvent` nodes | Append-only log + digital signature   |
| R-02 | Deny contract acceptance    | DSP             | Contract node with timestamp + DID     | Countersigned contract hash on ledger |

### Information Disclosure

| ID   | Threat                      | Component   | Demo Mitigation                   | Production Mitigation        |
| ---- | --------------------------- | ----------- | --------------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| I-01 | Patient data via unauth API | Next.js API | Role checks + middleware redirect | Same + network segmentation  |
| I-02 | Neo4j password in browser   | Next.js     | Server-side only env vars         | Vault + Kubernetes secrets   |
| I-03 | JWT in localStorage         | Browser     | **✅ Not stored (SEC-07 test)**   | HttpOnly cookie              |
| I-04 | XSS exfiltrates session     | Browser     | **✅ CSP header (D2)**            | Nonce-based CSP + SRI        |
| I-05 | Neo4j browser exposed       | Neo4j port  | Docker internal network           | No public exposure, VPN only |
| I-06 | Clickjacking                | Browser     | **✅ X-Frame-Options: DENY (D2)** | Same                         |

### Denial of Service

| ID   | Threat                   | Component          | Demo Mitigation           | Production Mitigation              |
| ---- | ------------------------ | ------------------ | ------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| D-01 | Unbounded Cypher queries | `/api/admin/audit` | `LIMIT $limit` (max 200)  | Rate limiting + query timeout      |
| D-02 | EDC flood via DSP        | ProviderEDC        | Demo has no rate limiting | EDC rate limiter + circuit breaker |
| D-03 | Large FHIR bundle        | neo4j-proxy        | Response size not capped  | Stream response + pagination       |

### Elevation of Privilege

| ID   | Threat                          | Component | Demo Mitigation                        | Production Mitigation                    |
| ---- | ------------------------------- | --------- | -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| E-01 | PATIENT accesses admin API      | Next.js   | Role check in `/api/admin/*` handlers  | Same + separate service account          |
| E-02 | DATA_USER reads PATIENT records | Next.js   | `/patient/*` middleware guards         | Attribute-based access control           |
| E-03 | Keycloak role injection         | JWT       | Roles mapped from Keycloak claims only | Claim whitelist + role schema validation |

---

## DSP 2025-1 Protocol Risks

| Risk   | Description                         | Demo Status                   | Mitigation                             |
| ------ | ----------------------------------- | ----------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| DSP-01 | Unsigned ContractAgreement messages | Consumer can forge acceptance | ⚠️ Not implemented                     | DID-signed messages per spec §5.3      |
| DSP-02 | No state machine enforcement        | STARTED→FINALIZED jump        | ⚠️ State stored in Neo4j, not enforced | Add state machine guard in ProviderEDC |
| DSP-03 | Transfer without active contract    | No contract reference check   | ⚠️ Seeded data assumes valid contracts | Validate `contractId` on each transfer |
| DSP-04 | Replay of transfer request          | Same `transferId` reused      | ⚠️ No nonce tracking                   | Idempotency key + TTL cache            |

---

## DCP v1.0 Protocol Risks

| Risk   | Description                | Demo Status                    | Mitigation                        |
| ------ | -------------------------- | ------------------------------ | --------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| DCP-01 | Unsigned VC presentation   | Forged participant attestation | ⚠️ Signature not verified in demo | Implement VC verification in TrustCenter |
| DCP-02 | Expired VC accepted        | `expirationDate` not checked   | ⚠️ Not checked                    | Add expiry check to `/api/credentials`   |
| DCP-03 | Revoked VC accepted        | No revocation list check       | ⚠️ Not implemented                | StatusList2021 or OCSP-style revocation  |
| DCP-04 | Credential schema mismatch | Wrong VC type accepted         | ⚠️ Type not validated             | Schema registry + type assertion         |

---

## Demo Phase Risk Register

| ID        | Risk                       | Likelihood           | Impact | Treatment             |
| --------- | -------------------------- | -------------------- | ------ | --------------------- |
| R-HIGH-01 | Cypher injection via audit | Low (fixed D1)       | HIGH   | ✅ Fixed              |
| R-HIGH-02 | Secrets in page HTML       | Low                  | HIGH   | ✅ SEC-10 test guards |
| R-MED-01  | Missing security headers   | Medium (was missing) | MEDIUM | ✅ Fixed D2           |
| R-MED-02  | Unsigned DSP messages      | High                 | MEDIUM | ⚠️ Accepted for demo  |
| R-MED-03  | VC signature not verified  | High                 | MEDIUM | ⚠️ Accepted for demo  |
| R-LOW-01  | No rate limiting on APIs   | High                 | LOW    | ⚠️ Accepted for demo  |

---

_Last updated: 2026-03-28 | Phase 23 — Demo Security Hardening_

# Threat model: Klarbefund, the iPhone app

The hub's threat model is [`threat-model.md`](/docs/security/threat-model-hub). This one is
for the app in `clients/ios`, which runs on a person's phone, holds their
laboratory values and sends nothing anywhere unless they say so. Written
2026-10-15 against commit `64737039`; each mitigation names the code or test
that shows it, and `clients/ios/Tests/SharedTests/SecurityPostureTests.swift`
pins the ones that are build settings. STRIDE, as in the hub's model.

## System context

```
   paper report ──camera──▶ ┌──────────────────────────────┐
   lab PDF ──files/share──▶ │ Klarbefund (iOS 26, Swift 6)  │
   Apple Health ──read───▶ │  OCR · coding · AES-GCM store │
                           └──────┬──────────┬────────────┘
                 optional, consent│          │optional, consent
                                  ▼          ▼
                 ┌──────────────────┐   ┌─────────────────────────┐
                 │ EHDS hub         │   │ explanation service      │
                 │ (ADR-049/054/057)│   │ on device by default;    │
                 │ OIDC+PKCE, App   │   │ hosted: Azure OpenAI EU  │
                 │ Attest, Bearer   │   │ data zone, or own key    │
                 └──────────────────┘   └─────────────────────────┘
```

Trust boundaries: the device (Secure Enclave, data protection, app sandbox)
is trusted as Apple provides it. Everything that leaves the device crosses a
boundary and does so only after a consent the person gave for that purpose.

## Assets

| Asset                                   | Where                                        | Why it matters                                         |
| --------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| Laboratory values, reports, page images | the store, `ReportStore.swift`               | Art. 9 GDPR health data                                |
| The store key                           | Keychain, `WhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly`       | decrypts everything above                              |
| Hub tokens (device grant, app token)    | Keychain, `ThisDeviceOnly`, `EHDSConnection` | write access to the person's own hub record            |
| App Attest key                          | Secure Enclave, `DeviceCheck`                | proves a genuine app to the hub when creating accounts |
| Consents and their history              | `Consents.swift`                             | the legal basis for every transfer                     |
| Diagnostics export                      | written on request only, ADR-038             | contains values; must never enter the repository       |

## STRIDE

### Spoofing

| Threat                                                    | Mitigation                                                                                                                           | Status |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------ |
| A fake app creates hub accounts or pushes data as the app | Account creation needs an Apple App Attest attestation the hub verifies (ADR-054); every later call carries the app token            | met    |
| A fake hub harvests tokens                                | OIDC discovery from the configured issuer only, PKCE S256, `ASWebAuthenticationSession`; ATS forbids plaintext (`OIDCSession.swift`) | met    |
| A fake explanation service reads values                   | The provider is named in the request the person approves (`CloudConsentSheet.swift`); HTTPS by ATS                                   | met    |
| Someone else at the unlocked phone                        | App lock: Face ID, Touch ID or the passcode before the cover lifts, on by default (`AppLock.swift`, ADR-060)                         | met    |

### Tampering

| Threat                                         | Mitigation                                                                                                            | Status   |
| ---------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
| Stored records altered on disk or over a cable | Each record AES-GCM sealed (authenticated), key in the Keychain; a cable test could not copy stored data              | met      |
| A misread value treated as a laboratory result | Provenance keeps OCR values `preliminary`; only a laboratory's own PDF text layer yields `final` (`Provenance.swift`) | met      |
| A tampered build                               | App Attest proves the app to the hub, not to itself; jailbreak and debugger detection declined with reasons (ADR-060) | accepted |
| A dependency with a backdoor                   | No third-party package at all (`Package.swift`, `project.yml`, `docs/sbom/klarbefund-ios.cdx.json`)                   | met      |

### Repudiation

| Threat                                | Mitigation                                                                                           | Status |
| ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------ |
| "I never consented to that transfer"  | Consent events with time, holder and effective date, revocable, with history (`Consents.swift`)      | met    |
| What was sent cannot be reconstructed | A sync is a FHIR Bundle with a SHA-256 fingerprint the app records (`EHDSConnection.swift`, ADR-057) | met    |

### Information disclosure

| Threat                                     | Mitigation                                                                                                                      | Status   |
| ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
| Values leave the device without the person | On-device OCR, coding, analysis and export; the only network calls are the two optional ones above, each behind its own consent | met      |
| Backups or iCloud carry the store          | Store excluded from backup; `NSFileProtectionComplete` default; exports and diagnostics written with complete protection        | met      |
| The app switcher shows values              | `PrivacyCover.swift` covers the window when the app is not active                                                               | met      |
| Logs carry values                          | Log lines carry counts and codes only (`Logging.swift`)                                                                         | met      |
| A cloud question identifies the person     | At most 40 values, no name, date of birth or insurance number; the service enforces the same (`CloudAnalysis.swift`, ADR-034)   | met      |
| Transfer to a third country                | Default on device; hosted default Azure OpenAI in the EU data zone; the Anthropic option is opt-in and says "United States"     | partly   |
| Screenshots or screen recording            | Not prevented (iOS allows no reliable block)                                                                                    | accepted |

### Denial of service

| Threat                           | Mitigation                                                                                                                             | Status   |
| -------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
| The hub is down                  | The app works without the hub; the record is on the device                                                                             | met      |
| A hostile scan floods the parser | Vision and the parser run on bounded images; a degraded scan loses rows, never hangs (`ScanningTests.swift`, `AccuracyBenchmarkTests`) | met      |
| Lost phone                       | Export in four formats for the person to keep; no recovery from the hub by design                                                      | accepted |

### Elevation of privilege

| Threat                                  | Mitigation                                                                                             | Status |
| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------ |
| Debug entry points in a release build   | `-MBSelfTest`, `-MBDemoSeed`, `-MBShot` are compiled out (`#if DEBUG`)                                 | met    |
| The app writes to Apple Health          | Read-only authorisation (`WearableSource.swift`); pinned by `SecurityPostureTests`                     | met    |
| The app token does more than the record | The hub scopes the token to the sandbox record of that account; `isSandboxUsername` on every app route | met    |

## Residual risks and what closes them

1. **App lock**: decided and implemented 2026-10-15 (ADR-060). (TR-03161 O.Auth)
2. **No tamper or jailbreak detection**: declined with reasons in ADR-060; the sealed store and App Attest are the controls. (O.Resi)
3. **No certificate pinning**: declined with reasons in ADR-060; ATS without an exception domain, managed rotation. (O.Ntwk)
4. **Hosted Anthropic option.** Opt-in, named on screen, but a transfer to the
   United States; the operator needs a transfer basis or must switch it off.
5. **Independent test.** This model and the tests are the project's own. An
   independent penetration test against a release build on a device, and the
   requirement-level TR-03161 gap list, remain open; see
   [`security-test-report-2026-10-15.md`](/docs/security/security-test-report).
